title: Statistical Simulation and Monte Carlo Methods
curriculum_locator: Stat H-307 Simulation & Monte Carlo Methods; University of Dhaka four-year B.S. Honours Statistics curriculum, starting session 2023–2024

units.title: Uniform Random Number Generation & Pseudorandom Foundations
scope: Principles of pseudorandom number generation: determinism, reproducibility, period length, and seed initialization
Linear Congruential Generators (LCG): modulus m, multiplier a, increment c, and Hull-Dobell Theorem for full period length
Multiplicative Congruential Generators (MCG) and maximal period conditions
Lattice structure of LCGs, Marsaglia's theorem on hyperplanes ('random numbers fall mainly in the planes')
Modern generators: Mersenne Twister (MT19937), Xorshift, and PCG (Permuted Congruential Generator)
Empirical statistical randomness testing batteries: frequency test, runs test, poker test, serial correlation test, NIST SP 800-22, and Dieharder test suite

units.title: Non-Uniform Random Variate Generation: Inversion & Transformations
scope: The Probability Integral Transform and Inverse Transform Method: continuous CDFs X = F^(-1)(U) and rigorous proofs
Discrete inverse transform sampling: table lookup, alias method (Walker's alias algorithm for O(1) sampling)
Transformation methods for continuous distributions: exponential, Weibull, Cauchy, Logistic, and Pareto variates
The Box-Muller transform for standard normal variates: polar coordinates derivation and Jacobian verification
Marsaglia-Bray polar method and rejection-polar optimization for Gaussian generation
Multivariate normal generation: mean vector mu, covariance matrix Sigma, and Cholesky decomposition X = mu + L Z

units.title: Rejection Sampling & Envelope Methods
scope: The Acceptance-Rejection Sampling Principle (Von Neumann): proposal density g(x), target density f(x), and bounding constant c
Mathematical proof of validity: marginal distribution of accepted candidates, acceptance probability P(accept) = 1/c
Optimal proposal selection and bounding constant minimization: c = sup_x [f(x)/g(x)]
Rejection sampling for standard distributions: generating Gamma variates using exponential or Cauchy proposals
Beta distribution sampling using uniform or triangular envelopes
Adaptive Rejection Sampling (ARS) for log-concave target densities: Gilks-Wild algorithm, upper/lower hulls, and rejection rate optimization

units.title: Monte Carlo Integration & Precision
scope: Foundations of Monte Carlo integration: estimating expected values and definite integrals theta = E[h(X)]
Unbiasedness of the Monte Carlo estimator theta_hat and consistency via the Strong Law of Large Numbers
Asymptotic standard error: sigma_hat / sqrt(n) and asymptotic Central Limit Theorem confidence intervals
Comparison of Monte Carlo convergence O(n^(-1/2)) with deterministic numerical quadrature (trapezoidal O(n^(-2/d)), Simpson's rule O(n^(-4/d)))
The curse of dimensionality in numerical integration and the asymptotic superiority of Monte Carlo in d >= 4 dimensions
Sample size determination for prespecified margin of error and relative error bounds

units.title: Variance Reduction Techniques
scope: Principles of variance reduction: efficiency improvements without increasing computational sample size
Antithetic Variates Method: negative covariance induction Cov(h(U), h(1-U)) < 0, monotonic transformations, and efficiency ratio
Control Variates Method: auxiliary variable Y with known expectation mu_Y, optimal correlation coefficient c* = Cov(X,Y)/Var(Y), and percentage variance reduction
Importance Sampling: change of measure, Radon-Nikodym derivative / likelihood ratio w(x) = f(x)/g(x), and optimal instrumental density g*(x) proportional to |h(x)|f(x)
Stratified Sampling: proportional vs Neyman optimal allocation of sample points across strata, and variance decomposition
Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS): multidimensional stratification, orthogonal arrays, and variance bounds

units.title: Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC): Metropolis-Hastings Algorithms
scope: Foundations of Markov chains: state space, transition kernels P(x, dy), stationarity, irreducibility, aperiodicity, and Harris recurrence
Detailed balance (reversibility) condition and invariance of target distribution pi(x)
The Metropolis-Hastings Algorithm: candidate proposal distribution q(y|x) and acceptance probability alpha(x, y) = min(1, [pi(y)q(x|y)]/[pi(x)q(y|x)])
Random-Walk Metropolis-Hastings: symmetric proposals q(y|x) = q(|x-y|) and Gaussian perturbation steps
Independence Sampler: q(y|x) = q(y) and geometric convergence conditions
Tuning candidate proposal dispersion: the Roberts-Gelman-Gilks optimal acceptance rate rule (0.234 for multidimensional targets)
MCMC Convergence diagnostics: trace plots, autocorrelation functions (ACF), burn-in periods, Gelman-Rubin potential scale reduction factor R_hat, and Effective Sample Size (ESS)

units.title: The Gibbs Sampler & Bayesian Computational Inference
scope: The Gibbs Sampler as a special case of Metropolis-Hastings with acceptance probability identically equal to 1.0
Full conditional posterior distributions pi(theta_i | theta_(-i), y) and componentwise updates
Systematic scan vs random scan Gibbs sampling: transition kernels and convergence properties
Data augmentation and latent variable simulation (Tanner & Wong framework)
Gibbs sampling implementation for normal-normal conjugate models and Bayesian multiple linear regression with conjugate priors
Bayesian Probit regression using Albert-Chib latent Gaussian data augmentation
Hierarchical models: random-effects modeling and variance component estimation via Gibbs sampling

units.title: Resampling & Permutation Methods: Bootstrap and Jackknife
scope: The Plug-in Principle and Bradley Efron's Empirical Bootstrap: drawing resamples with replacement from empirical distribution F_hat_n
Non-parametric bootstrap for standard error estimation, bias estimation, and sampling distribution approximation
Parametric bootstrap: simulating from estimated parametric families F_hat_theta
Bootstrap confidence intervals: standard normal approximation, basic bootstrap intervals, percentile bootstrap intervals, and studentized bootstrap-t
Bias-Corrected and Accelerated (BCa) bootstrap confidence intervals: acceleration parameter a and bias-correction factor z_0
The Quenouille-Tukey Jackknife: leave-one-out pseudovalues, jackknife bias estimator, and variance estimator
Permutation tests: Fisher's exact test of independence, two-sample permutation tests, and exact Monte Carlo p-value computation
